lucknow-muzaffarpur-highway-land.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project upgraded 328 km of NH-28 to a four-lane divided road, after the target was cut from the 483 km planned at approval. Travel time along the corridor fell 23 per cent for cars and 25 per cent for trucks against a 20 per cent target, and fatal accidents fell 36 per cent corridor-wide; but the target of a 10 per cent cut in truck operating costs was met in none of the three sections, and on the Ayodhya-Gorakhpur section fatal accidents rose from 22 a year to 43. The Bank put the economic rate of return at 26 per cent, which it describes as measuring savings in vehicle operating costs and passenger travel time, not gains to anyone whose land was taken. The completion report rated the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory; the Bank's Independent Evaluation Group rated it Unsatisfactory, rated Bank performance Unsatisfactory against the report's Moderately Unsatisfactory, and rated the project's monitoring Negligible. No figures from outside the Bank were found.
lucknow-muzaffarpur-highway-land.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report (13 Dec 2012, results table and paras 55-62, Annex 3) and the Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR14100 (posted 5 Feb 2014), both read in full from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

mekenajo-dembidolo-road-coffee.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the programme upgraded about 302 km of narrow gravel road to asphalt, against the 391 km targeted, after the 89 km Ankober-Dulecha-Awash Arba road was dropped. On the 181 km Mekenajo-Dembidolo road, traffic rose 330 per cent after the upgrade, average travel time fell from three minutes a kilometre in 2009 to one minute in 2017, and minibus waiting time fell from 112.6 minutes in 2012 to 23.5 minutes in 2016. The Bank put that road's economic rate of return at 21.5 per cent after the fact against 14.8 per cent at appraisal, describing it as measuring savings in vehicle operating costs, maintenance and travel time; contracts overran their budgets by about 30 per cent on average and their time by about 140 per cent. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group both rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, with the Group rating the quality of monitoring Modest against the report's Substantial and noting that the wider figures cited for road condition and rural access reflect the whole government road programme rather than this project.
mekenajo-dembidolo-road-coffee.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004205 (1 Jun 2018) and the Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR0021231, read in full from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

naji-youjiang-waterways-resettlement.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the Naji complex delivered a shiplock and a hydropower station whose installed capacity was raised during design from 57 to 66 megawatts, with three turbines finished in 2008, though full-capacity generation waited two years for resettlement and reservoir filling; the plant was expected to average 273 GWh a year against 253 GWh assumed at appraisal. Waterway freight between Baise and Nanning reached 2.4 million tonnes in 2009, up from 0.8 million tonnes in 2003 and 9.9 per cent above the year's target, and average ship size rose from 97 to 144.7 deadweight tonnes against a target of 152. The Bank put the Guangxi component's economic rate of return at 15.8 per cent at completion against 18 per cent at appraisal, noting that no document trail survived for the appraisal assumptions, so the two are hard to compare; the financial rate of return fell from the 3.4 per cent estimated at appraisal to 0.74 per cent after lock fees along the Xijiang were abolished and power was sold below the assumed price. The completion report records farm incomes in Tianyang County rising from RMB 1,923 in 2004 to RMB 3,579 in 2009; the Independent Evaluation Group adds that it is not clear how much of that can be attributed to the project.
naji-youjiang-waterways-resettlement.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR1376 (28 Dec 2011) and the Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR13857 (posted 14 Jan 2013), read in full from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

nanguang-railway-resettlement.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built about 400 km of double-track electrified railway between Litang West and New Zhaoqing plus two tracks of a 62 km four-track line on to Sanyanqiao, with 94 million man-days of temporary construction work, most of the hired labour coming from Guangxi rather than the richer Guangdong. Express train pairs between the two regions rose from seven to 31 against a target of 20 and journey time fell from 620 minutes to 156 minutes against a target of 170; the eight pairs of daily freight trains targeted never ran, because China Railway chose to keep freight on the conventional line. The Bank put the economic rate of return at 16 per cent after the fact against 13 per cent at appraisal, and its Independent Evaluation Group, which visited the line in March 2018, found that about half of the counted benefit came not from transport savings but from modelled 'agglomeration' effects, estimated using a method from the United Kingdom's Department for Transport. The completion report, the Group's desk review and the Group's 2018 field assessment all rated the outcome Satisfactory; the Group records income and land-value rises along the line but says there was no counterfactual, so the project's share in them cannot be separated from inflation and other causes.
nanguang-railway-resettlement.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR3432 (3 Dec 2015), Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR0020097 and Group Project Performance Assessment Report 127580 (2018), read from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

nhiip-india-corridor-land-acquisition.whole: By the World Bank's own count, average travel time on the project roads fell from two minutes a kilometre to 1.17 for cars and from three minutes to 1.7 for trucks, both better than target, and recorded road deaths fell 45 per cent from a baseline of 163 in 2009; vehicle operating costs fell from Rs 8 to Rs 7.2 a kilometre for cars and Rs 14 to Rs 12.6 for trucks, figures the Independent Evaluation Group says there is not enough evidence to show were checked against other data. The Bank put the economic rate of return at 20.3 per cent for the eight completed sections totalling 617 km, against 25.74 per cent estimated at appraisal for the full 1,200 km, attributing the drop to contract delays, lower traffic and higher costs, and describing it as measuring savings in vehicle operating costs, maintenance and travel time. A road-safety enforcement pilot budgeted at US$72.5 million spent US$3.2 million, and the Group concludes it was not carried out. The Group also says the improvement claimed in the share of state roads in good condition cannot be attributed to the project, because the classified network itself grew from 37,501 km to 87,995 km.
nhiip-india-corridor-land-acquisition.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report (29 Jun 2022) and Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review (21 Feb 2023) for P121185, read in full from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

orissa-state-roads-compensation.whole: Two of the project's six roads were finished. On those two the Bank's own measurements show vehicle speeds up 32.5 per cent against a 36 per cent target, and it recorded no data at all for vehicle operating cost savings; the project did deliver a road asset management system the state was using to plan maintenance budgets by closing, a road network master plan, a road safety policy and a study on creating a road fund, while a road sector policy was written but not adopted. The Bank's economic rate of return for the two completed roads was 19.4 per cent for Khariar-Bhawanipatna and 18.6 per cent for Berhampur-Taptapani, against 22.3 and 15.4 per cent estimated for them at appraisal, with construction unit costs 1.6 to 1.8 times the appraisal estimate offset by traffic growing two to three times faster than assumed. The Bank's Independent Evaluation Group rated the project's achievement of its objective Negligible and its outcome Unsatisfactory, against the completion report's Moderately Unsatisfactory, writing that the project did not remove transport bottlenecks, that there is no evidence congestion was reduced, and that the effect on investment and development was never measured.
orissa-state-roads-compensation.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report for P096023 (Feb 2017, paras 57-59, Table 4, Annex 3) and the Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review (21 Jun 2017), read in full from the PDFs. The Group's efficiency section states the ex-post and appraisal returns in the reverse order to its own ratings table and to the completion report, so only the per-road figures both documents agree on are given here; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

shaanxi-ankang-road-resettlement.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built an 87 km expressway from Ankang to Maoba and rehabilitated 106 local roads totalling 1,391.75 km, against 108 roads and about 1,480 km expected at appraisal. Travel time from Ankang to Maoba fell from 3.8 hours on the old parallel highways to one hour, and daily traffic on the sample county and township roads rose from 243 vehicles in 2009 to 508 in 2012. Traffic on the new expressway reached 3,049 vehicles a day in 2012, short of the 6,585 target, because tolls on the two parallel roads were removed in 2011 and traffic moved to them; accidents on the new expressway numbered 126 in 2012 against a target of 35, with two deaths against a target of 13. The Bank put the economic rate of return at 15.3 per cent against 17.9 per cent at appraisal, describing it as measuring savings in vehicle operating costs and passenger travel time; the expressway cost US$1,096 million, 95 per cent above the appraisal estimate.
shaanxi-ankang-road-resettlement.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR2142 (13 Jun 2013) and the Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review for P075613 (22 Sep 2014), read in full from the PDFs. The expressway length is the completion report's 87 km (para, p.565 of the text layer) and 1,391.75 km of local roads from its output table; the Group's review prints 78 km, apparently a transposition. No non-Bank source with output figures was found.

shiyan-connecting-road-safeguards.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built the 106.4 km four-lane Shiyan-Manchuanguan Expressway, opened to traffic in December 2007 with the tunnel at the Shaanxi border opening in October 2009, together with 262 km of local roads in four stretches and the 355 metre Jiangjunhe bridge, which replaced an old bridge that carried only single-file traffic. Two of the local roads had previously been earth tracks closed 45 and 90 days a year; bus service frequency on the local roads rose four to five times, and traffic on the expressway reached 6,600 to 8,700 vehicles a day by early 2010, meeting or exceeding targets at the counting stations. The recorded fatal accident rate fell from 3.4 to 3.1 per million vehicle-kilometres against a target of 2.9, and the Bank put the cost-weighted economic rate of return at 19 per cent against 17 per cent at appraisal, covering savings in vehicle operating costs and travel time. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group both rated the outcome Satisfactory; the Group records an 80 per cent rise in the counties' GDP alongside the roads and says the improvements were not wholly due to the road upgrading.
shiyan-connecting-road-safeguards.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR1409 for P081749 (Annex 2 outputs table, Annex 3) and the Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review for P081749, read from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

shizheng-railway-resettlement.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built 355 km of new double-track high-speed railway between Shijiazhuang and Zhengzhou and eight stations against a target of six, and bought 28 catenary maintenance vehicles. Journey time for non-stop high-speed trains fell from 198 minutes before the project to 81 minutes, better than the 85-minute target, and passenger density on the corridor rose from 61 million passenger-route kilometres in 2012 to 75 million in 2014, of which the new line carried 23 million. The corridor carried 180 train pairs a day in 2015 against the 181 forecast at appraisal, but with 60 high-speed pairs instead of the 100 assumed, because the government kept more trains running on the conventional line for social reasons; trains ran at 310 km/h rather than the 350 km/h first operated, to cut energy use. The Bank put the economic rate of return at 15 per cent after the fact against 20 per cent at appraisal, describing it as measuring travel-time savings, capacity freed on the old line and reduced road accidents and emissions; the Independent Evaluation Group rated the risk to the result Modest against the report's Negligible, judging the social risk modest because passenger attitude surveys may not reflect what people can actually pay.
shizheng-railway-resettlement.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00003435 (18 Oct 2016) and the Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review for P099062 (8 Mar 2017), read from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

vietnam-distribution-efficiency-five-hou.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project built or reinforced 8,587 km of high-, medium- and low-voltage line and 4,742 MVA of substation capacity, and carried out 177 subprojects against the 99 planned at appraisal, savings on procurement paying for the rest. Distribution losses across the five power corporations fell by between 1.6 and 7.5 percentage points more than targeted; metered customers cut consumption by a combined 448.5 GWh a year against a 414.5 GWh target, and avoided emissions came to 365,707 tonnes of CO2 a year against a target of 269,148. The Bank put the economic rate of return at 38.3 per cent at completion against 29.2 per cent estimated at appraisal for the first phase, and the financial return to the power companies at 19.7 per cent against 16.7 per cent, crediting lower costs and a wider margin between the bulk supply and retail tariffs. The completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group both rated the outcome Highly Satisfactory; the Group notes that the report does not discuss what the retail tariff increases meant for households, and that over 2005 to 2019 average tariffs rose 53 per cent while cumulative inflation was about 56 per cent.
vietnam-distribution-efficiency-five-hou.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report for P125996 (14 Jun 2019) and the Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review for P125996 (21 Jan 2020), read in full from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

vietnam-rural-energy-2-land-loss.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project installed 27,700 circuit km of low-voltage line against a revised 32,000 km target, 5,300 circuit km of medium-voltage line against 4,300 targeted, 700 MVA of transformer capacity against 1,100 targeted, and 1,915,000 household meters against 2,700,000 targeted. Household access to electricity in the project provinces rose from 60 per cent to 98 per cent, with 325,000 households in remote areas connected across 25 provinces; average low-voltage distribution losses fell from 30 per cent to 10 per cent, and recorded carbon savings were 365,000 tonnes against a 310,000 tonne target. The Bank put the economic rate of return at 17.5 per cent against 18.2 per cent at appraisal, a figure covering reduced losses, cheaper grid power replacing costlier sources and higher sales; unit investment cost per household rose from US$578 in 2005 to US$1,062 in 2009. The project's stated aim was to support the social and economic development of rural communities, and the Independent Evaluation Group records that no study was carried out at closure to assess whether it did.
vietnam-rural-energy-2-land-loss.searched: World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR3194 for P074688 and the Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR14722 (12 May 2015), read in full from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.

vietnam-water-resources-assistance-reset.whole: By the World Bank's own count, the project rehabilitated and modernised six irrigation schemes under 295 construction contracts, raising the share of each scheme's command area actually irrigated from 50 per cent to 81 per cent against a 75 per cent target; annual crop production rose 31 per cent for paddy, 41 per cent for maize, 52 per cent for soybean and 94 per cent for vegetables. It also set up a dam safety unit covering the ministry that oversees about 95 per cent of Vietnam's dams, carried out remedial works on four dams, and issued a national dam safety regulation. The Bank put the economic rate of return at about 15 per cent measured on agricultural benefits from irrigation, and gave a wider figure of 27.7 per cent when municipal and industrial water use was included; farm income on a typical 0.25 hectare fully irrigated farm rose from about US$46 to US$103 a year. The completion report, the Independent Evaluation Group's desk review and the Group's 2019 field assessment all rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, the review stating that much of the production increase came from irrigating more land rather than from the modernisation the project was built around, and the 2019 assessment recording about a third less infrastructure completed than originally planned and productivity gains that relied partly on government extension work outside the project.
vietnam-water-resources-assistance-reset.searched: Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR14273 (9 Dec 2013) and Group Project Performance Assessment Report 13838 (20 Aug 2019) for P065898, read from the PDFs; no non-Bank source with output figures was found.
